text:
emily-cs: hey folks — DataFlow reporting intermittent 503s on hosted inference between 10:15–10:25 PST. They see ~30% requests failing with 503s and long tails. customer says failures align with auth-heavy spikes. attaching a small log excerpt from their request ids

emily-cs: ```
2026-03-17T17:15:12Z request_id=aa11 status=200 latency_ms=120
2026-03-17T17:15:13Z request_id=aa12 status=503 upstream_exit=137 runner=runner-172
2026-03-17T17:15:14Z request_id=aa13 status=503 upstream_signal=SIGILL
2026-03-17T17:15:15Z request_id=aa14 status=200 latency_ms=98
```

devon-oncall: thanks, picking this up. I see correlated restarts in our cluster: runner-172 shows repeated hot-restart cycles starting 17:14:55Z. quick grep shows `Illegal instruction (core dumped)` in the container logs. rolling up logs now.

shreya-eng-runtime: @devon can you paste the container log tail? curious if it's a kernel SIGILL or from JIT/quant kernel. also which model/quant config was running.

devon-oncall: ```
Mar 17 17:14:55 runner-172[pid=4271]: runtime: hot-restart initiated
Mar 17 17:14:55 runner-172[pid=4271]: error: kernel_launch returned 192 (invalid instruction)
Mar 17 17:14:55 runner-172[pid=4271]: signal: SIGILL (core dumped)
Mar 17 17:14:56 runner-172: container restarted by kubelet
Mar 17 17:14:58 runner-172[pid=4302]: loading model redwood-v1-quantized fp16
Mar 17 17:15:03 runner-172[pid=4302]: error: nvml: ECC single-bit corrected on GPU0
```

michael-infra: NVML ECC messages are interesting — ECC corrected shouldn't SIGILL but could indicate underlying GPU driver instability. I pulled driver dmesg: `GPU 0000:af:00.0: pcie error: fatal - status 0x1` around the same time.

shreya-eng-runtime: model was `redwood-v1-quantized` with fused kernels enabled + custom cuBLAS patch. SIGILL inside compiled kernel usually means mismatch between compiled PTX and driver/SM version (or memory corruption). Did we recently roll kernel patches?

devon-oncall: we rolled a micro-compiler patch to fused-attn kernels yesterday at 03:00 UTC (7742a2 -> 7742b6). Only a subset of pools got the patch (canary). This runner is in the canary pool.

emily-cs: customer wants ETA and workaround — they can redirect traffic to other regions but need guidance.

shreya-eng-runtime: immediate mitigation: 1) remove runner from canary (evict) 2) route DataFlow to fallback model variant (non-fused kernels) OR pin to a different model shard. I've created a quick routing override we can apply.

michael-infra: applying eviction now to cluster-canary-1. devon, I'll also taint the node to prevent scheduling until further notice.

support-bot: action logged: incident-INC-2026-0317-1 created; paging eng-runtime.

devon-oncall: repro steps to validate locally:
```bash
# reproduce auth-heavy spike with 64 concurrent tokens
for i in {1..64}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://hosted.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
# watch runner logs
kubectl -n infer logs -l app=runner -c runner -f --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
```

shreya-eng-runtime: additional debug: if you can grab a core dump from the container before it's removed, run `gdb --batch -ex "bt" /opt/runner/bin/runner core` and capture the backtrace. early trace we got from a core:
```
#0  0x00007f9cabc12345 in fused_attn_kernel(float*, float*, ...)
#1  0x00007f9caa9f0abc in run_inference_loop
#2  0x0000555a12bcdeff in main
```
kernel SIGILL at offset 0x12345 inside the fused-attn PTX.

michael-infra: logs show this only in canary nodes with driver version 525.85.12 and CUDA 12.2. production pool nodes are on driver 526.x. might be a driver/PTX mismatch after the compiler patch.

emily-cs: told customer we'll route them to us-west-2 fallback and keep them updated. they asked if this is a billing exposure (retries causing duplicate tokens).

devon-oncall: for now mark the failing requests as retriable in routing layer but throttle immediate retries to avoid double-billing. CS note: we'll waive duplicated token charges between 17:14–17:25 for DataFlow.

shreya-eng-runtime: long term: revert the fused-attn micro-patch for canary, run a PTX rebuild against driver 525 and 526, and add a runtime check to refuse incompatible kernels (detect SM version mismatch at load time). I'll open a PR and a rollback.

michael-infra: done: node tainted, runners evicted from canary-1. rolling restart of canary pool to roll back compiler artifacts.

devon-oncall: monitoring: I'm watching p95/p99 and runner restart counts. early signal: drops to baseline after eviction. will post update in 10m.

emily-cs: thanks. I'll update DataFlow support channel with the workaround and the billing note.

shreya-eng-runtime: ACTIONS:
- shreya: open PR to revert micro-compiler patch + add compatibility guard (link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/XXXX)
- devon: keep monitoring, collect any remaining cores (save to s3://core-archives/canary/8401234567/)
- michael: run cross-driver PTX rebuild test matrix on staging (525, 526)
- emily-cs: confirm billing waiver with finance and update customer thread

support-bot: incident status -> acknowledged (priority: high).

devon-oncall: update: 17:24Z — runner restarts stopped, error rate for DataFlow down to 0.5% from 30%. closing the support escalation unless new errors surface.

emily-cs: customer confirmed fallback routing succeeded. closing their ticket after billing waiver note. thanks all :thumbsup:
